es.summary: La EAP es la reducción del flujo sanguíneo a extremidades por aterosclerosis de arterias periféricas, produciendo isquemia crónica.
key_points: El tabaquismo es el factor de riesgo más fuerte.
Claudicación intermitente es el síntoma clásico.
Control de factores de riesgo y ejercicio son esenciales.

pathophysiology: Acumulación de placa de colesterol y grasa en la íntima arterial.
Estrechamiento del lumen arterial reduce el flujo sanguíneo distal.
Isquemia tisular durante la actividad física genera dolor muscular.
En casos graves, la falta de perfusión produce ulceración y gangrena.
risk_factors: Edad > 65 años y antecedentes de enfermedad cardiovascular.
signs_symptoms: Claudicación intermitente: dolor en piernas al caminar >100‑200 m.
Dolor en reposo o nocturno en etapas avanzadas.
Piel pálida, cianótica o fría al tacto.
Úlceras o heridas que cicatrizan lentamente en pies y tobillos.
diagnostics: Doppler arterial y ecografía Doppler para flujo y estenosis.
Angiografía por tomografía o resonancia si se considera revascularización.
Perfil lipídico, glucosa en ayunas y hemoglobina glicosilada para factores de riesgo.
treatment: Cese del tabaquismo y terapia de reemplazo nicotínico.
Aspirina o clopidogrel para prevención de trombosis.
Control de presión arterial y glucemia.
nursing_care: Evaluar pulsos pedales, tiempo de relleno capilar y temperatura de la piel.
Inspeccionar diariamente pies y uñas en busca de lesiones.
Monitorear ITB y registrar cambios en la marcha.
Fomentar programa de caminata progresiva y registrar distancia sin dolor.
Educar sobre cese de tabaco y adherencia a medicación.
Cuidar heridas: desbridamiento suave, apósitos húmedos y control de infección.
patient_teaching: Dejar de fumar: recursos de cesación y terapia de reemplazo.
Realizar caminatas diarias, aumentando gradualmente la distancia.
Inspeccionar pies cada mañana; reportar heridas o cambios de color.
Usar calzado cómodo y sin costuras que no comprima los dedos.
Mantener control regular de presión arterial, glucosa y lípidos.
Acudir a citas de seguimiento para pruebas de perfusión.

evidenced_by: limitación de la distancia de marcha
outcomes: Tolerancia a la actividad: caminar 200 m sin dolor en 2 semanas
Dolor durante la actividad: escala ≤3/10 en 1 mes

interventions.action: Evaluar dolor antes, durante y después de la caminata usando escala numérica.
interventions.rationale: Permite medir la intensidad y la respuesta al ejercicio.

interventions.action: Diseñar un programa de caminata progresiva, aumentando 10 m cada sesión.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la circulación colateral y reduce la claudicación.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de reposo activo (sentarse y elevar piernas) al inicio del dolor.
interventions.rationale: Alivia la isquemia temporal y permite continuar la actividad.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y pulsos pedales cada visita.
interventions.rationale: Detecta deterioro de la perfusión que pueda limitar la actividad.

interventions.action: Reforzar la educación sobre cese de tabaco y adherencia a estatinas.
interventions.rationale: Reduce progresión de la aterosclerosis y mejora la tolerancia al ejercicio.

en.summary: PAD is the reduction of blood flow to the limbs due to atherosclerosis of peripheral arteries, causing chronic ischemia.
key_points: Smoking is the strongest risk factor.
Intermittent claudication is the classic symptom.
Risk factor control and exercise are essential.

pathophysiology: Accumulation of cholesterol and fat plaque in the arterial intima.
Arterial lumen narrowing reduces distal blood flow.
Tissue ischemia during physical activity causes muscle pain.
In severe cases, lack of perfusion leads to ulceration and gangrene.
risk_factors: Age >65 years and history of cardiovascular disease.
signs_symptoms: Intermittent claudication: leg pain when walking >100‑200 m.
Rest or nocturnal pain in advanced stages.
Pale, cyanotic or cold skin to touch.
Ulcers or wounds that heal slowly on feet and ankles.
diagnostics: Arterial Doppler and Doppler ultrasound for flow and stenosis.
CT or MR angiography if revascularization is considered.
Lipid profile, fasting glucose and hemoglobin A1c for risk factors.
treatment: Smoking cessation and nicotine replacement therapy.
Aspirin or clopidogrel for thrombosis prevention.
nursing_care: Assess pedal pulses, capillary refill time and skin temperature.
Inspect feet and nails daily for lesions.
Monitor ABI and record changes in gait.
Encourage progressive walking program and record pain‑free distance.
Educate on smoking cessation and medication adherence.
Wound care: gentle debridement, moist dressings and infection control.
patient_teaching: Quit smoking: cessation resources and replacement therapy.
Inspect feet each morning; report wounds or color changes.
Wear comfortable, non‑stitched shoes that do not compress toes.
Maintain regular monitoring of blood pressure, glucose and lipids.
Attend follow‑up appointments for perfusion tests.

outcomes: Activity tolerance: walk 200 m pain‑free in 2 weeks
Pain during activity: scale ≤3/10 in 1 month

interventions.action: Assess pain before, during, and after walking using a numeric scale.
interventions.rationale: Allows measurement of intensity and response to exercise.

interventions.action: Design a progressive walking program, increasing 10 m each session.
interventions.rationale: Improves collateral circulation and reduces claudication.

interventions.action: Teach the patient active rest techniques (sitting and elevating legs) at pain onset.
interventions.rationale: Relieves temporary ischemia and allows continuation of activity.

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and pedal pulses at each visit.
interventions.rationale: Detects perfusion deterioration that may limit activity.

interventions.action: Reinforce education on smoking cessation and statin adherence.
interventions.rationale: Reduces atherosclerosis progression and improves exercise tolerance.

sources.name: Clinical Nursing Skills: Peripheral Vascular System

summary.0.quote: Arterial insufficiency occurs when arterial blood flow is reduced due to atherosclerotic blockages.

key_points.0.quote: The cause of PAD is atherosclerosis .

key_points.1.quote: The main risk factor for PAD is smoking.

key_points.2.quote: A primary symptom of peripheral vascular disease is intermittent claudication , a cramp-like muscle pain, burning sensation, or extreme fatigue in the calf, thigh, or buttocks that is induced by exercise and relieved by rest.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Plaque is a substance made up of fat and cholesterol.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Reduced blood flow from atherosclerotic blockages is known as peripheral arterial disease .

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: When arterial blood is obstructed by narrowed, constricted vessels ( Figure 12.31 , the legs encounter a perfusion defect, and the patient may experience pain during ambulation, which is known as intermittent claudication .

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: The main risk factor for PAD is smoking.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Other risk factors include older age and diseases like diabetes, high blood cholesterol, high blood pressure, heart disease, and stroke.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Weak or absent pulses in the legs or feet

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: On assessment, the affected limb may feel cold to touch, pulses may be weak, and the skin will exhibit color changes such as pallor or decreased capillary refill due to insufficient blood getting to the limbs from arterial insufficiency.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Sores or wounds on the toes, feet, or legs that heal slowly, poorly, or not at all

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Doppler Ultrasound (National Library of Medicine) Also in Spanish

sections.treatment.3.quote: Chronic pharmacological management will consist of statin therapy to avoid further plaque formation.

sections.complications.2.quote: Atherosclerosis Thickening or hardening of the arteries over time Potential heart attack or stroke

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: On assessment, the affected limb may feel cold to touch, pulses may be weak, and the skin will exhibit color changes such as pallor or decreased capillary refill due to insufficient blood getting to the limbs from arterial insufficiency.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: The patient will demonstrate compliance with a healthy lifestyle and adherence to the medication regimen.
